title: [AUG-148] Transcribe a video or audio file from a pasted direct http(s) link
why_we_need_this: Meeting recordings are often shared as links (public S3/CDN URLs, Dropbox `?dl=1`, direct .mp4/.mov/.mp3 links) rather than files. Today the user must download the file and then upload it again. Letting August fetch the file itself removes that step, and the promise holds: August only downloads, and transcription stays local. AUG-144 already turns any downloaded .mp4/.mov/audio file into a transcript.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The upload panel in @client/src/components/FileUpload.tsx has a "Paste link" input (brutalist, 0 border-radius) that accepts an http(s) URL and starts transcription in the selected language.
- [ ] New endpoint (e.g. POST /api/sessions/from-url { url, language }) creates a session titled with the file name from the URL (or Content-Disposition), downloads into the session folder as audio.{ext}, then runs the existing pipeline (ensureWav → transcribe), including the AUG-144 video handling.
- [ ] The response returns right after the session is created; the download runs in the background with visible progress (percent when Content-Length is known) and Cancel aborts it and removes the partial file.
- [ ] Accepted only when the scheme is http/https and the media type is supported: extension in UPLOAD_EXTENSIONS (@server/src/services/mediaFormats.ts) or a Content-Type of audio/* / video/mp4 / video/quicktime. HTML pages (e.g. a YouTube or Drive viewer page) fail with "This link is not a direct media file — download it and upload the file instead."
- [ ] Downloads stop at a size cap (2 GB, same as uploads) and on a network timeout, with a clear message. The session ends up failed, with "Transcribe again" available where the file was fully saved.
- [ ] Safety: only http/https; redirects are followed but capped (≤5) and re-validated; loopback, link-local and private-network addresses are refused unless the user confirms (no silent requests into the local network).
- [ ] Packaged desktop builds download through the existing fetch override (electron.net.fetch), so the system proxy and certificate store apply; verified on Windows and reasoned for macOS.
- [ ] Retranscribe works on a link-sourced session using the downloaded file (no re-download).
- [ ] Verified with: a direct .mp4 link, a direct .mp3 link, a Dropbox `?dl=1` link, a YouTube page URL (rejected with the message), a 404 link and a cancelled download.
- [ ] project-context/transcription/README.md documents the link flow, accepted links, limits and safety rules.
important_constraints:
- Direct file links only. Video-site extraction (YouTube, Vimeo, Loom via yt-dlp) and private links (Zoom cloud, Google Drive, SharePoint) are out of scope — a separate decision.
- No new npm dependency for downloading; reuse the shared streaming download helper (download.ts: downloadToFile) if it fits, otherwise native fetch streaming.
- Transcription stays local whisper only; never send the URL or the media to a third-party service.
- A failed download or transcription never deletes a fully downloaded source file.
- Both platforms; use path.join and config paths, no hardcoded binary names.
- Order: best done after AUG-147 (background "preparing" phase) so download and extraction share the same phase and Cancel; if done first, the endpoint must still respond immediately. Related: AUG-144, AUG-145 (size limit message).
